turns.t: Good morning. I'll be as precise as I can, because this is a bit unusual. My cousin died suddenly last month, aged thirty-one, and I'd like to be screened.
I'm very sorry to hear that. Do you know what the cause was?
They say it was his heart, an arrhythmia of some kind. They're still waiting for the full post-mortem results.
That must be very hard on the family. And how about you, have you had any symptoms yourself? ~
Possibly. Now and then I get a flutter in my chest, a sort of skipped beat. But I can't say when I first noticed it.
Is it when you're resting, or exercising?
Resting, usually. It might have been last year, or the year before, I honestly couldn't tell you.
Do you ever faint, or nearly faint, with it?
No, never. I've never fainted in my life.
Good. Do you exercise much?
I run three times a week, five kilometres, and I've never had trouble with it.
That's reassuring. Any allergies I need to know about before I examine you?
None at all. No allergies.
Let me take your pulse and blood pressure. ~
Of course. ~
Pulse 62, regular, and blood pressure 118 over 74.
Is that normal? ~
Excellent for a runner. ~
So what do you think the flutter is? ~
A skipped beat at rest, in someone who runs and has a normal pulse, is most likely ectopic beats, which are extra beats and very common.
Common? So not necessarily a problem? ~
Usually harmless. But with your cousin's history, I don't want to rely on that. ~
Quite. That's why I came. ~
I'm going to refer you to the inherited cardiac conditions clinic, and they'll do the right tests, probably an ECG, an echocardiogram, and maybe a heart rhythm monitor.
And the cousin's results will matter? ~
Very much. Ask the family to share the post-mortem findings with the clinic, they'll want to see them.
I'll do that. Is there anything I should avoid in the meantime? ~
Carry on as normal, and if you ever faint, or get chest pain with exercise, or a racing heart that won't settle, go to the emergency department.
Understood. Thank you for being so thorough. ~
You did the right thing. The clinic will write to you. ~

chief_complaint.normalized_value: Cardiac screening after relative's sudden death

clinical_actions.description: Refer to inherited cardiac conditions clinic
Ask family to share post-mortem findings with the clinic
Safety-net: emergency department if fainting, exertional chest pain or racing heart

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient could not say when the chest flutter first began ("last year, or the year before").
